tagline: Gold-country Ophir and a forest trail meeting at Flint Hill Road
intro: Flint Hill Road meets Ophir Road in Ophir, a community in the Uwharrie National Forest. NCDOT includes Flint Hill Ramble among its scenic byways, a program intended to offer alternatives to major highways and to introduce the state’s history, geography and culture.

Ophir was settled during North Carolina’s mid-nineteenth-century gold boom and named for the biblical gold-producing region associated with Solomon’s temple. A later route through this country was made for walking: Scoutmaster Joe Moffitt began the northern Uwharrie Trail in the late 1960s.

Begin with Ophir and its Uwharrie River setting. Flint Hill Road also reaches the Jumpin Off Rock trailhead, where northern and southern trail-building efforts met to complete a 40-mile hiking route in 1975.

moments.title: Ophir
moments.text: Ophir’s name belongs to its gold-boom origins: it refers to the biblical region that supplied gold for King Solomon’s temple. The community was settled in the mid-nineteenth century. Just west, the Steel Mine lay along the Uwharrie River. An English company bought the property in 1876, and ore was treated in Chilean mills until 1884. By 1934, a ten-stamp mill, boiler, engine and roaster remained on the site, deteriorating. The mine’s ore included thin seams of free gold alongside galena, sphalerite, chalcopyrite and pyrite. Production records are fragmentary and based on estimates.

moments.title: Uwharrie Trail
moments.text: Joe Moffitt wanted a local fifty-mile hike so his Asheboro Scouts could earn their 50 Miler award. In the late 1960s, he began assembling the northern Uwharrie Trail from Tot Hill Road through the Birkhead to Flint Hill Road at Jumping Off Rock. Gaps in public ownership later made the route vulnerable: land changed hands and access disappeared in many places. Volunteers, the LandTrust for Central NC and the Forest Service have worked since 1998 to reconnect the fragmented trail. A trailhead at Little Long Mountain’s base was named for Moffitt in 2013, recognizing his work as a Scout leader and trail pioneer.

moments.title: Jumping Off Rock
moments.text: Jumpin Off Rock trailhead on Flint Hill Road marks the northern end of the Uwharrie National Recreation Trail’s 20.5-mile southern section. From here, that section extends to NC 24/27. An 8.5-mile section between Jumpin Off Rock and High Pine Church Road opened to the public in spring 2021, restoring part of the longer trail northward.

sources.label: North Carolina Department of Transportation, North Carolina Scenic Byways, fifth edition
